subject.title: feat: ask_user — structured questions from the agent with web card, channel buttons, and text answers

question: Should question RPCs reuse an existing operator scope to preserve all paired clients, or should OpenClaw introduce `operator.questions` with an explicit device-token upgrade path?
rationale: Operator scopes are persisted authorization contracts, and automation cannot choose whether this capability belongs inside the existing write boundary or merits a new least-privilege scope that requires user-visible reapproval.

options.title: Reuse `operator.write`
options.body: Gate question creation, lookup, resolution, and events with the existing write scope so upgraded paired clients continue connecting without a new approval.

options.title: Ship a new question scope
options.body: Keep `operator.questions`, but add explicit pairing-upgrade UX or migration guidance, update scope documentation and bootstrap contracts, and prove fresh-install plus existing-device upgrades.

recommendation.title: Reuse `operator.write`
recommendation.body: Gate question creation, lookup, resolution, and events with the existing write scope so upgraded paired clients continue connecting without a new approval.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the merged predecessor and has the strongest recent history around Gateway operator-scope upgrade behavior.
